newsitem.title: USA: Leading U.S. House Democrat wants China MFN revoked.
newsitem.headline: Leading U.S. House Democrat wants China MFN revoked.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt said on Tuesday that U.S. trade policy with China has failed and called on Congress to revoke Beijing's trading privileges.

"Our trade policy with China has failed," Gephardt said in a speech prepared for delivery to the Detroit Economic Club. "It has failed not only on moral grounds, but economically as well. There is nothing 'free' about our trade with China -- in fact it comes to us at great cost and little benefit."
Gephardt noted the U.S. trade deficit with China was almost $40 billion last year and said it is projected to exceed $50 billion this year. A copy of the speech was made available in Washington.

He criticized President Bill Clinton's policy of engagement with China saying it has been "far too weak" and said the time had come for Washington to take a firmer stance toward Beijing on human rights and other issues.

"A new policy of firm engagement can and must begin next month when the U.S. Congress will review Most Favored Nation trading status for China," Gephardt said. "This market access is a privilege, not a right. I believe that the communist government in Beijing has forfeited that privilege. It is time we revoke China's Most Favored Nation status."

China's trading status is reviewed annually and Clinton decided last week to renew MFN for another year. Congress may vote to reject that decision. Without MFN, tariffs on imports from China would soar to the high levels of the 1930's. Only a handful of countries are denied MFN trade privileges.
